claims.statement: The batibat is a vengeful demon of Ilocano folklore, called bangungot in Tagalog folklore, taking the form of an ancient, grossly obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.
claims.statement_id: Batibat adalah setan pendendam dalam cerita rakyat Ilokano, disebut bangungot dalam cerita rakyat Tagalog, berwujud roh perempuan tua yang sangat gemuk penghuni pohon.
claims.quote: The Batibat is a vengeful demon found in Ilocano folklore. In Tagalog folklore, the creature is called Bangungot. The batibat takes the form of an ancient, grotesquely obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

claims.statement: Batibat usually meet humans when their trees are felled, especially when made into a house post, and then inhabit what is left of the tree.
claims.statement_id: Batibat biasanya bersentuhan dengan manusia ketika pohonnya ditebang, terutama bila dijadikan tiang rumah, lalu ia menghuni sisa pohonnya.
claims.quote: They usually come in contact with humans when the trees in which they reside are felled and are made homeless, especially when their tree is made into a support post for a house.

claims.statement: The batibat forbids sleeping near its post; if someone does, it takes its true form, smothers the victim and invades their dreams, causing sleep paralysis and nightmares; hence the Ilocano word batíbat for nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Batibat melarang manusia tidur di dekat tiangnya; bila ada yang tidur di sana, ia berubah ke wujud aslinya, menindih korban dan memasuki mimpinya hingga terjadi ketindihan dan mimpi buruk; dari sinilah kata Ilokano batíbat untuk mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: When a person does sleep near it, the batibat transforms into its true form and attacks the person by suffocating their victim and invading their dream space, causing sleep paralysis and waking nightmares. This condition lends itself to the Ilocano word for nightmare, "batíbat"

claims.statement: To ward off the batibat, bite your thumb or wiggle your toes to wake from the nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menangkal batibat, orang dianjurkan menggigit ibu jari atau menggerakkan jari kaki agar terbangun dari mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: To ward off the batibat, one should bite one's thumb or wiggle one's toes. In this way, the person will awaken from the nightmare induced by the batibat.

claims.statement: The creature appears in the fifth episode of the Netflix series Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, played by Megan Leitch.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini muncul dalam episode kelima serial Netflix Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, diperankan Megan Leitch.
claims.quote: The creature appears in the fifth episode of the Netflix series Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, played by Megan Leitch.

claims.statement: The 2020 horror film Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat features one of these creatures.
claims.statement_id: Film horor Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat (2020) menampilkan makhluk ini.
claims.quote: The 2020 horror film Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat features one of these creatures.

claims.statement: These spirits are blamed as the cause of the fatal nocturnal disease called bangungot, or SUNDS (sudden unexplained nocturnal death syndrome).
claims.statement_id: Roh-roh ini disalahkan sebagai penyebab penyakit malam hari yang mematikan bernama bangungot atau SUNDS (sindrom kematian malam hari mendadak tanpa sebab yang jelas).
claims.quote: These spirits are blamed as the cause of the fatal nocturnal disease called bangungot or *SUNDS (sudden unexplained nocturnal death syndrome).

claims.statement: A batibat takes the form of a huge, old, fat woman who resides in trees; when such trees are cut down for house posts, the home owner may find they have inherited an unwanted guest.
claims.statement_id: Batibat berwujud perempuan tua yang besar dan gemuk dan tinggal di pohon; bila pohon itu ditebang untuk dijadikan tiang rumah, pemilik rumah bisa mendapati bahwa ia mewarisi tamu yang tidak diinginkan.
claims.quote: A Batibat takes the form of a huge, old, fat woman that resides in trees. When these trees are cut down to make posts for a house, the home owner may find that they have inherited an unwanted guest.

claims.statement: The batibat migrates into holes in the posts and gets particularly cranky when someone dares to sleep near it; it transforms and sits on the chest of its victim until he suffocates.
claims.statement_id: Batibat berpindah ke lubang-lubang pada tiang dan menjadi sangat gusar bila ada yang berani tidur di dekatnya; ia berubah wujud dan duduk di dada korbannya sampai korban sesak napas.
claims.quote: The Batibat migrates into holes found in the posts and gets particularly cranky when someone dares to sleep near it. The Batibat will transform and sit on the chest of its victim until he suffocates.

claims.statement: In the case of the batibat, nobody would have the option of a heroic battle: she is believed to be so heavy and large that even the burliest of men would be suffocated under her mass.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kasus batibat, tak seorang pun punya kesempatan melawan secara heroik: ia dipercaya begitu berat dan besar sehingga lelaki paling kekar pun akan sesak napas di bawah tubuhnya.
claims.quote: In the case of the Batibat, nobody would have the option of a heroic battle – she is believed to be so heavy and large, that even the burliest of men would be suffocated under her mass.

claims.statement: The batibat can be warded off by biting your thumb or wiggling your toes, which apparently wakes you from a batibat-induced nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Batibat dapat ditangkal dengan menggigit ibu jari atau menggerakkan jari kaki, yang konon membangunkan orang dari mimpi buruk akibat batibat.
claims.quote: you can ward off the batibat by biting your thumb or wiggle your toes – which will apparently wake you up from a Batibat induced nightmare.

claims.statement: In the Philippines, SUNDS is called bangungot in the vernacular and affects 43 per 100,000 each year among young Filipinos; most victims are male.
claims.statement_id: Di Filipina, SUNDS disebut bangungot dalam bahasa sehari-hari dan menimpa 43 per 100.000 orang tiap tahun di kalangan orang Filipina muda; sebagian besar korbannya laki-laki.
claims.quote: In the Philippines, where it is referred to in the vernacular as bangungot, SUNDS affects 43 per 100,000 each year among young Filipinos. Most of the victims are males.

claims.statement: According to the article, doctors recently found a trend among men who died from bangungot: they consumed a lot of starchy food and alcohol right before going to bed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, dokter akhir-akhir ini menemukan pola pada pria yang meninggal karena bangungot: mereka makan banyak makanan bertepung dan minum alkohol tepat sebelum tidur.
claims.quote: In recent years, doctors have discovered a trend with the men who have died from bangungot – they consumed a lot of starchy food and alcohol right before they went to bed.

claims.statement: The article author argues that an enormous angry spirit smothering a sleeper was a better answer than doctors saying "we don't know", and that in the case of SUNDS the batibat offered closure to those who lost a loved one.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis artikel, roh raksasa yang marah dan menindih orang tidur terasa lebih baik daripada jawaban dokter "kami tidak tahu"; bagi keluarga yang kehilangan, batibat memberi penutup atas kematian akibat SUNDS.
claims.quote: An enormous angry spirit smothering a person in their sleep was still a better answer than doctors offering, 'we don't know'. Closure can be important for those who lose a loved one, and in the case of SUNDS, the Batibat offered it.

claims.statement: In the recap of the Sabrina episode, Batibat is revealed as the demon Sabrina accidentally freed in the prior episode after solving her father's puzzle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam resensi episode serial Sabrina, batibat diungkap sebagai iblis yang tanpa sengaja dibebaskan Sabrina pada episode sebelumnya setelah ia memecahkan teka-teki milik ayahnya.
claims.quote: Batibat is revealed as the demon Sabrina accidentally freed in the prior episode after solving her father's puzzle.

claims.statement: In the series, the demon gets trapped in the Spellman house, which is what it wants, since it is trying to get revenge on the Spellmans.
claims.statement_id: Dalam serial itu, iblis tersebut terperangkap di rumah keluarga Spellman, yang memang diinginkannya karena ia berusaha membalas dendam kepada keluarga Spellman.
claims.quote: The demon gets trapped in the Spellman house, which is actually what it wants, since it's trying to get revenge on Spellmans.

claims.statement: A batibat named Maganda is referenced in the eleventh episode of Lost Girl's second season, "Can't see the Fae-Rest", as a Balinese tree nymph.
claims.statement_id: Seorang batibat bernama Maganda disebut dalam episode kesebelas musim kedua Lost Girl, berjudul "Can't see the Fae-Rest", sebagai nimfa pohon Bali.
claims.quote: A Batibat named Maganda is referenced in the eleventh episode of Lost Girl's second season, titled "Can't see the Fae-Rest" as a Balinese tree nymph.

claims.statement: The bungisngis is a one-eyed giant of Philippine folklore said to live in Meluz, Orion, Bataan and Batangas and always laughing; its name comes from Cebuano ngisi, 'to giggle'.
claims.statement_id: Bungisngis adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam cerita rakyat Filipina yang konon tinggal di Meluz, Orion, Bataan, dan Batangas dan selalu tertawa; namanya berasal dari kata Cebuano ngisi, 'terkikik'.
claims.quote: Bungisngis is a one-eyed giant in Philippine folklore. This giant, purported to dwell in Meluz, Orion, Bataan and Batangas and is described as always laughing. The literal meaning of the name Bungingis is derived from the Cebuano word ngisi which means "to giggle".

claims.statement: This humanlike giant has always-visible large teeth, an upper lip covering its face when thrown back, two long tusks, and a single mid-forehead eye offset by sharp hearing.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa berwujud manusia ini bergigi besar yang selalu terlihat, bibir atasnya menutupi wajah saat mendongak, dua taring panjang mencuat dari mulutnya, dan satu-satunya matanya di tengah dahi diimbangi pendengaran tajam.
claims.quote: Having a humanoid shape, it has large teeth which are always showing, and its upper lip covers its face when it is thrown back. Two long tusks protrude from the sides of its mouth. The giant's only eye is found in the middle of its forehead, but this is compensated for by its strong sense of hearing.

claims.statement: In the Filipino tale The Three Friends: the Monkey, the Dog and the Carabao, the giant lifts the carabao and throws it knee-deep into the ground; though strong, it is easily outwitted and panics, and the Monkey's tricks lead to its death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Filipina Tiga Sahabat: Monyet, Anjing, dan Kerbau, raksasa ini mengangkat kerbau dan melemparnya hingga terbenam sampai lutut; meski kuat, bungisngis mudah diakali dan cepat panik, dan tipu daya Monyet membawanya pada kematian.
claims.quote: In the Filipino tale "The Three Friends – The Monkey, The Dog and The Carabao," the giant is able to lift the carabao and throw it with such force that it lands knee-deep in the ground. However, despite its strength, the bungisngis is easily outwitted and quickly panics.

claims.statement: The tale "The Three Friends: The Monkey, the Dog, and the Carabao" in Fansler's collection was narrated by José M. Hilario, a Tagalog from Batangas.
claims.statement_id: Kisah "Tiga Sahabat: Monyet, Anjing, dan Kerbau" dalam kumpulan Fansler dituturkan oleh José M. Hilario, orang Tagalog dari Batangas.
claims.quote: The Three Friends,--The Monkey, the Dog, and the Carabao. Narrated by José M. Hilario, a Tagalog from Batangas, Batangas.

claims.statement: In the tale, the Buñgisñgis in the forest hears the noise of frying, goes up to the carabao to fill his stomach and says the carabao has prepared food for him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, Buñgisñgis di hutan mendengar bunyi daging digoreng, lalu mendatangi kerbau untuk mengisi perutnya dan berkata bahwa kerbau telah menyiapkan makanan untuknya.
claims.quote: Unfortunately the noise of the frying was heard by the Buñgisñgis in the forest. Seeing this chance to fill his stomach, the Buñgisñgis went up to the carabao, and said, "Well, friend, I see that you have prepared food for me."

claims.statement: When the carabao attacked him, the Buñgisñgis was angered, seized the carabao by the horn and threw him knee-deep into the earth, then ate all the food and disappeared.
claims.statement_id: Ketika kerbau menyerangnya, Buñgisñgis marah, memegang kerbau pada tanduknya dan melemparnya sampai terbenam sedalam lutut ke tanah, lalu menghabiskan semua makanan dan menghilang.
claims.quote: For an answer, the carabao made a furious attack on him. The Buñgisñgis was angered by the carabao's lack of hospitality, and, seizing him by the horn, threw him knee-deep into the earth. Then the Buñgisñgis ate up all the food and disappeared.

claims.statement: The Buñgisñgis did not dare attack all three friends at once, for in union there is strength.
claims.statement_id: Buñgisñgis tidak berani menyerang ketiga sahabat sekaligus karena persatuan adalah kekuatan.
claims.quote: The Buñgisñgis saw them cooking, but he did not dare attack all three of them at once, for in union there is strength.

claims.statement: The monkey jerked a leg of the chair, sending the Buñgisñgis tumbling into the pit, and then filled the pit with earth.
claims.statement_id: Monyet menarik kaki kursi sehingga Buñgisñgis jatuh ke dalam lubang, lalu menimbunnya dengan tanah.
claims.quote: The monkey took hold of a leg of the chair, gave a jerk, and sent his guest tumbling into the pit. He then filled the pit with earth, so that the Buñgisñgis was buried with no solemnity.

claims.statement: The Buñgisñgis was still alive; he jumped out, killed the dog and lamed the carabao, while the monkey escaped by climbing a tree.
claims.statement_id: Buñgisñgis ternyata masih hidup, melompat keluar, membunuh si anjing dan membuat si kerbau pincang, sedangkan si monyet lolos dengan memanjat pohon.
claims.quote: Unfortunately the Buñgisñgis was still alive. He jumped out, and killed the dog and lamed the carabao; but the monkey climbed up a tree, and so escaped.

claims.statement: Becoming impatient, the Buñgisñgis pulled the vine, and the bees immediately buzzed about him and punished him for his curiosity.
claims.statement_id: Karena tidak sabar, Buñgisñgis menarik sulur, dan lebah-lebah segera berdengung di sekelilingnya serta menghukumnya atas rasa ingin tahunya.
claims.quote: the Buñgisñgis, becoming impatient, pulled the vine. The bees immediately buzzed about him, and punished him for his curiosity.

claims.statement: The monkey placed the boa-constrictor around the Buñgisñgis's body and pinched the boa, which soon made an end of his enemy.
claims.statement_id: Si monyet melilitkan boa ke tubuh Buñgisñgis lalu mencubit ular itu, dan boa itu segera mengakhiri hidup musuhnya.
claims.quote: The monkey placed the boa-constrictor around the body of the Buñgisñgis. Then he pinched the boa, which soon made an end of his enemy.

claims.statement: According to the notes, the narrator defines Buñgisñgis as "a large strong man that is always laughing", and the word derives from the root ñgisi, "to show the teeth" (Tag.).
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Fansler, penutur mengartikan Buñgisñgis sebagai "seorang lelaki besar dan kuat yang selalu tertawa", dan katanya berasal dari akar ñgisi, "menunjukkan gigi" (Tag.).
claims.quote: Buñgisñgis is defined by the narrator as meaning "a large strong man that is always laughing." The word is derived from the root ñgisi, "to show the teeth" (Tag.).

claims.statement: According to the notes, this giant is described as of herculean size and strength, sly, with an upper lip so large that when thrown back it covers the face completely; it can lift a huge animal as easily as a feather.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Fansler, raksasa ini digambarkan berukuran dan berkekuatan seperti Herkules, licik, dan berbibir atas sebesar itu sehingga bila disingkapkan ke belakang menutupi seluruh wajah; ia mampu mengangkat hewan besar semudah mengangkat bulu.
claims.quote: This giant has been described to me as being of herculean size and strength, sly, and possessing an upper lip so large that when it is thrown back it completely covers the demon's face. The Buñgisñgis can lift a huge animal as easily as if it were a feather.

claims.statement: Fansler's notes state that the two superhuman demons of these tales, the Buñgisñgis among them, have to be overcome with strategy, not muscle, so the heroes are beings endowed with cleverness.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Fansler menyatakan bahwa kedua iblis adikuasa dalam kisah-kisah itu, termasuk Buñgisñgis, harus dikalahkan dengan siasat, bukan otot, sehingga pahlawannya adalah makhluk yang cerdik.
claims.quote: The Buñgisñgis can lift a huge animal as easily as if it were a feather. ... Obviously these two superhuman demons have to be overcome with strategy, not muscle. The heroes, consequently, are beings endowed with cleverness.

claims.statement: According to the Aswang Project article, the Bungisngis's origin is easy to trace thanks to a similar being in the Ibalong Epic, where the cyclopean giant is called Buring, while in the Hindu epic it is called Kabandha.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Aswang Project, asal-usul Bungisngis mudah dilacak berkat makhluk serupa dalam Epos Ibalong, tempat raksasa bermata satu itu disebut Buring, sedangkan dalam epos Hindu disebut Kabandha.
claims.quote: Tracing the origin of the Bungisngis was actually quite easy, thanks to a similar being existing in the Ibalong Epic. ... In the Ibalong, the cyclopean giant is known as “Buring“, while in the Hindu epic it is known as “Kabandha”.

claims.statement: In the Batangas tale, the Bungisngis was led by his hearing to where a carabao was frying meat in the woods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah dari Batangas, Bungisngis dituntun oleh pendengarannya ke tempat seekor kerbau menggoreng daging di hutan.
claims.quote: In the Batangas tale, Bungisngis was led by his hearing to where a carabao was frying meat in the woods.

claims.statement: According to the Aswang Project, the Bungisngis is not part of a Batangas epic but plays a central role in the folk story "The Three Friends: The Monkey, the Dog, and the Carabao".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Aswang Project, Bungisngis bukan bagian dari epos Batangas, tetapi berperan sentral dalam cerita rakyat "Tiga Sahabat: Monyet, Anjing, dan Kerbau".
claims.quote: While the Bungisngis is not part of a Batangas epic, it does play a central role in the folk story, “The Three Friends,–The Monkey, the Dog, and the Carabao.“

issues.message: Di bawah target rich: 1 penerbit selain Wikipedia (target 2; Wikipedia semua bahasa dihitung satu). gaps sudah diisi; nilai apakah pencariannya memadai.

claims.statement: Cha kla (จะกละ) or Phi Cha kla is a spirit of Thai folklore resembling a wild cat, believed to be a malevolent spirit raised and controlled by warlocks to harm enemies; in southern Thailand it is called phi luang.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla (จะกละ) atau Phi Cha kla adalah roh dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang menyerupai kucing liar, diyakini roh jahat yang dipelihara dan dikendalikan penyihir untuk mencelakai musuh; di Thailand selatan disebut phi luang.
claims.quote: or Phi Cha kla (ผีจะกละ, pronounced [pʰiː t͡ɕà kà.lá]) is a type of spirit in Thai folklore, said to resemble a wild cat. It is believed to be a malevolent spirit raised and controlled by warlocks to harm their enemies. In the southern regions of Thailand, it is known as phi luang

claims.statement: Cha kla is recorded in the Ayutthaya-period Three Seals Law Code, over 300 years old, alongside beings such as the krasue, under the name cha la.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla tercatat dalam Hukum Tiga Segel dari masa Ayutthaya, lebih dari 300 tahun lalu, bersama makhluk gaib lain seperti krasue, dengan nama cha la.
claims.quote: It is documented in the Three Seals Law Code dating back over 300 years to the Ayutthaya period, where it is listed alongside other supernatural beings such as the Krasue. In the text, it is referred to as Cha la

claims.statement: Cha kla's fur is pitch black, coarse and dull, growing backwards upward and forward, its eyes blood-red; it emerges only at night, fears humans and flees to its burrow when seen.
claims.statement_id: Bulu cha kla hitam pekat, kasar, dan kusam, tumbuh terbalik ke atas dan ke depan, matanya merah seperti darah; ia hanya keluar malam hari, takut manusia, dan lari ke liangnya bila terlihat.
claims.quote: However, its fur is pitch black with a coarse texture, lacking any shine. The hairs grow in reverse, flaring upward and forward. Its eyes glow deep red, like blood. Nocturnal by nature, Cha kla emerges only at night. It fears humans

claims.statement: According to legend, cha kla has a deadly aura; merely seeing or touching it can cause death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, cha kla memiliki aura mematikan; melihat atau menyentuhnya saja dapat menyebabkan kematian.
claims.quote: According to legend, Cha kla possesses a deadly aura. Even the mere sight or touch of it can cause death.

claims.statement: At first glance, the cha kla may appear no different from a normal house cat.
claims.statement_id: Sekilas, cha kla tampak tidak berbeda dari kucing rumah biasa.
claims.quote: At first glance, Cha kla may appear no different from a normal house cat.

claims.statement: The cha kla fears humans, and whenever it encounters people or is spotted by people, it immediately flees into its burrow.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla takut pada manusia, dan setiap bertemu orang atau terlihat orang, ia segera lari masuk ke liangnya.
claims.quote: It fears humans, and whenever it encounters people, or when people spot it, it immediately flees into its burrow.

claims.statement: These creatures are said to dig underground holes for shelter, rarely venturing out during the day.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon menggali lubang di bawah tanah sebagai tempat berlindung dan jarang keluar pada siang hari.
claims.quote: These creatures are said to dig underground holes for shelter, rarely venturing out during the day.

claims.statement: Cha kla is considered a traditional Thai ghost belief with long-standing roots.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla dianggap sebagai kepercayaan hantu tradisional Thailand yang berakar lama.
claims.quote: Cha kla is considered a traditional Thai ghost belief with long-standing roots.

claims.statement: A case was said to have occurred in Krabi province where an entire family was found dead at home; according to medical reports the official cause was "sudden cardiac failure", but the victims' relatives believed it was the work of the cha kla.
claims.statement_id: Konon pernah terjadi di Provinsi Krabi satu keluarga ditemukan tewas di rumahnya; menurut laporan medis penyebab resminya adalah "gagal jantung mendadak", tetapi kerabat korban meyakini itu perbuatan cha kla.
claims.quote: One such chilling event was said to have occurred in Krabi province, where an entire family was found dead in their home. The official cause, according to medical reports, was "sudden cardiac failure". However, the victims' relatives believed it was the work of Cha kla.

claims.statement: On investigating the house, a strange deep burrow was found behind it, with tufts of black fur around its entrance, believed to be from a cat.
claims.statement_id: Ketika rumah itu diperiksa, ditemukan liang dalam yang aneh di belakangnya, dan di sekitar mulut liang terdapat gumpalan bulu hitam yang diduga bulu kucing.
claims.quote: Upon investigating the house, they found a strange deep burrow behind it, and around the entrance were tufts of black fur, believed to be from a cat.

claims.statement: The journal article glosses cha kla (จะกละ) as a kind of ghost believed to take the form of a cat, living in the forest, kept by forest sorcerers to harm enemies, and a type of ghost that likes to eat filth.
claims.statement_id: Artikel jurnal ini memberi definisi: cha kla (จะกละ) adalah sejenis hantu yang dipercaya berwujud kucing, tinggal di hutan, dipelihara dukun hutan untuk mencelakai musuh, dan sejenis hantu yang suka makan barang kotor.
claims.quote: จะกละ (ชื่อผีชนิดหนึ่ง เชื่อกันวEามีรูปเปUนแมว อยูEในปXาซึ่งหมอผีชาวปXาเลี้ยงไวPใหPทํา รPายศัตรู, ผีพวกหนึ่งชอบกินของโสโครก)

claims.statement: The journal article says the Phra Aiyakan Betset section on chomop, cha kla, krasue and krahang has 20 articles, covering among other things accusing, reviling and slandering someone of being these ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Artikel jurnal ini menyebut bagian hukum Phra Aiyakan Betset tentang chomop, cha kla, krasue, dan krahang berisi 20 pasal, antara lain tentang tuduhan, cacian, dan fitnah bahwa seseorang adalah hantu-hantu itu.
claims.quote: พระอัยการเบ็ดเสร็จวEาดPวยเรื่องฉมบ จะกละ กระสือ และกระหาง 20 มาตรา ไดPแกE การกลEาวหา ดEา วEา ตูE วEาเปUนฉมบ จะกละ กระสือ กระหาง การทํายาเบื่อยาเมายาแฝด

claims.statement: According to the article, an accusation that someone is a chomop, cha kla, krasue or krahang was an important charge requiring proof, because it was a form of social punishment that made people fear and shun the accused.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, tuduhan bahwa seseorang adalah chomop, cha kla, krasue, atau krahang merupakan tuduhan penting yang harus dibuktikan, karena menjadi hukuman sosial yang membuat orang takut dan tidak mau bergaul.

claims.statement_id: Artikel jurnal ini menyebut phi ka atau phi cha kla (ผีกะ หรือ ผีจะกละ) sebagai hantu yang suka merasuki orang agar menuntut makanan; orang yang dirasuki bertingkah tidak wajar dan memakan makanan dengan rakus.
claims.quote: ผีกะ หรือ ผีจะกละ เป็น ผี ที่ มั ก เข้ า สิ งผู้ ค นเพื่ อ เรี ย กร้ อ งจะกิ น อาหารเมื่ อ เข้ า สิ งใคร ก็ จ ะแสดงกิ ริ ย าผิ ด ปกติ ไป เมื่ อ คน สังเกตเห็นก็มักร้องขอกินอาหารและจะกินอย่างตะกละตะกลาม

claims.statement: Khamot (โขมด) is a ghost of Thai folklore; its name is borrowed from Khmer khmaoch, 'ghost in general', and it is considered related to the krasue and phong ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Khamot (โขมด) adalah hantu dalam cerita rakyat Thailand; namanya dipinjam dari kata Khmer khmaoch, 'hantu secara umum', dan ia dianggap berkerabat dengan krasue dan hantu phong.
claims.quote: is a type of ghost in Thai folklore. The term is borrowed from the Khmer word khmaoch

claims.statement: In some accounts khamot appears as a floating, flickering light at night, especially in damp or marshy areas, misleading forest travellers into thinking someone ahead carries a torch or there is a fire; approached, it vanishes and reappears all around.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian kisah khamot tampak sebagai bola cahaya melayang yang berkedip di malam hari, terutama di daerah lembap atau berawa, dan menyesatkan pengembara di hutan seolah ada orang membawa obor atau api di depan; saat didekati cahaya itu lenyap lalu muncul mengelilingi.
claims.quote: In some accounts, it appears as a floating ball of light, a large flickering glow seen at night, especially in damp or marshy areas. It is said to lure travelers in the forest into losing their way, making them believe that someone ahead is carrying a torch or that there is a fire.

claims.statement: Per the Royal Institute Dictionary, the phenomenon is scientifically explained as methane from decaying organic matter igniting in the air; it also groups khamot with the krasue and phong ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kamus Royal Institute, secara ilmiah gejala ini dijelaskan sebagai gas metana dari pembusukan bahan organik yang dapat menyala di udara; kamus itu juga menggolongkan khamot bersama krasue dan hantu phong.
claims.quote: Scientifically, this phenomenon is explained as methane gas produced by the decomposition of organic matter, which can ignite in the air and appear as flickering lights in the dark.

claims.statement: In some regions khamot is a forest spirit seen as floating light; in others a malevolent ghost deceiving travellers by shapeshifting.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah khamot dianggap roh hutan berupa cahaya melayang, di daerah lain hantu jahat yang menipu pengembara dengan berganti wujud.
claims.quote: In others, it is considered a malevolent ghost that deceives and haunts travelers by shapeshifting into various forms.

claims.statement: In Lamphun, northern Thailand, the Loy Khamot tradition is held at the twelfth lunar month's full moon, coinciding with Loy Krathong, with floating lanterns sparkling like khamot's lights.
claims.statement_id: Di Provinsi Lamphun, Thailand utara, ada tradisi Loy Khamot pada purnama bulan kedua belas, bertepatan dengan Loy Krathong, dengan lentera terapung yang berkilau seperti cahaya khamot.
claims.quote: In Lamphun province, northern Thailand, there is a local tradition called Loy Khamot (ลอยโขมด), held during the full moon of the twelfth lunar month, which coincides with the Loy Krathong festival

claims.statement: The khamot has no definite form; in some accounts it appears as a floating ball of light, a large flickering glow seen at night, especially in damp or marshy areas.
claims.statement_id: Khamot tidak berwujud tetap; dalam sebagian kisah ia tampak sebagai bola cahaya melayang, pendar besar yang berkedip pada malam hari, terutama di daerah lembap atau berawa.
claims.quote: It has no definite form. In some accounts, it appears as a floating ball of light, a large flickering glow seen at night, especially in damp or marshy areas.

claims.statement: When travelers approach, the light suddenly disappears, only to reappear surrounding them from all directions.
claims.statement_id: Ketika para pelancong mendekat, cahaya itu tiba-tiba lenyap lalu muncul kembali mengelilingi mereka dari segala arah.
claims.quote: When they approach, the light suddenly disappears, only to reappear surrounding them from all directions.

claims.statement: In some regions, the khamot is described as a type of forest spirit that manifests as a floating light at night.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah, khamot digambarkan sebagai sejenis roh hutan yang menampakkan diri sebagai cahaya melayang pada malam hari.
claims.quote: In some regions, it is described as a type of forest spirit that manifests as a floating light at night.

claims.statement: The khamot is considered a spirit related to the krasue and phong ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Khamot dianggap roh yang berkerabat dengan hantu krasue dan phong.
claims.quote: It is considered a spirit related to Krasue and Phong ghosts.

claims.statement: According to the Thai Fine Arts Department site, the khamot (ผีโขมด) is a name for a forest ghost that goes out at night, with a glow of fire seen at intervals like the krasue ghost; hence the Lanna people call the floating-lantern festival "loy khamot".
claims.statement_id: Menurut situs Departemen Seni Rupa Thailand, khamot (ผีโขมด) adalah nama hantu hutan yang keluar mencari makan pada malam hari, dengan kobaran api yang terlihat sesekali seperti hantu krasue; karena itu orang Lanna menyebut perayaan lampu apung itu "loy khamot".
claims.quote: ทำให้เกิดแสงแวววาวกระทบกับผิวน้ำในคืนวันเพ็ญคล้ายกับดวงไฟของผีโขมด ซึ่งผีโขมดนี้ เป็นชื่อเรียก ผีป่า ที่ออกหากินในเวลากลางคืน มีพะเนียงไฟมองเห็นเป็นระยะอย่างผีกระสือ ชาวล้านนา จึงเรียกว่า ลอยโขมด

claims.statement: The loy khamot festival is held by villagers of Ban Ton Thong, Mueang district, Lamphun, and nearby areas on the full-moon night of the Lanna second month (twelfth month); villagers make banana-stem krathong and float them on the Kuang River in front of Wat Romaniyaram with lit candles.
claims.statement_id: Perayaan loy khamot diadakan warga Ban Ton Thong, Kabupaten Mueang, Lamphun, dan sekitarnya pada malam bulan purnama bulan kedua Lanna (bulan kedua belas); warga membuat krathong dari pelepah pisang, lalu menghanyutkannya di Sungai Kuang di depan Wat Romaniyaram dengan lilin menyala.
claims.quote: ประเพณีลอยโขมดเป็นประเพณีที่ชาวบ้านต้นธง ต.ต้นธง อ.เมือง จ.ลำพูน รวมถึงชาวบ้านในพื้นที่ใกล้เคียง จัดขึ้นในช่วงยี่คืนวันเพ็ญในเดือนยี่เป็ง หรือเพ็ญเดือนสิบสอง ชาวบ้านจะมีการนำกาบกล้วยมาทำเป็นกระทงทรงกระโจมสำหรับใส่สิ่งของต่างๆ ลอยไปตามลำน้ำกวงบริเวณหน้าวัดรมณียาราม หรือวัดกู่ระมัก ในเวลากลางคืนพร้อมทั้งจุดเทียนไปในกระทงนั้นด้วย

claims.statement: The loy khamot festival is believed to originate from the legend of Chamthewi Wong, the chronicle of Hariphunchai, and the Jinakalamali, composed in the Lanna period.
claims.statement_id: Perayaan loy khamot dipercaya berasal dari legenda Chamthewi Wong, kronik kota Hariphunchai, dan Chinakalamali yang disusun pada masa Lanna.
claims.quote: ประเพณีการลอยโขมดเชื่อว่ามีต้นเค้ามาจากตำนานจามเทววีวงศ์ พงศาวดารเมืองหริภุญไชย และชินกาลมาลีนี ที่แต่งขึ้นในสมัยล้านนา

claims.statement: According to the Trang national library, the khamot is a kind of forest ghost often appearing as a light at night that vanishes when approached; some say it is a fierce forest ghost that can take various forms and haunts people walking in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut perpustakaan nasional cabang Trang, khamot adalah sejenis hantu hutan yang sering tampak sebagai cahaya pada malam hari dan lenyap bila didekati; sebagian orang menyebutnya hantu hutan galak yang dapat menampakkan berbagai rupa dan menghantui pejalan di hutan.
claims.quote: ๔. ผีโขมด เป็นผีป่าชนิดหนึ่ง มักปรากฏเป็นดวงไฟในยามค่ำคืน เมื่อเข้าใกล้จะหายไป บ้างก็ว่าเป็นผีป่าดุร้าย ปรากฏรูปร่างได้ต่างๆ หลอกหลอนคนเดินป่า

claims.statement: The journal article states that khamot is the name of a forest ghost that likes to go out at night and appears as an intermittent glow of fire like the krasue ghost.
claims.statement_id: Artikel jurnal ini menyatakan bahwa kata khamot adalah nama hantu hutan yang suka keluar mencari makan pada malam hari dan tampak sebagai kobaran api sesekali seperti hantu krasue.
claims.quote: ลอยโขมด คำว่า โขมด เป็นชื่อผีป่า เรียกกันว่า ผีโขมด ชอบออกหากินกลางคืน จะมี พะเนียงไฟเห็นเป็นระยะอย่างผีกระสือ

claims.statement: According to the article's abstract, the significance of the loy khamot festival is to float away misfortune and sin, letting the misfortunes in oneself flow away with the water during the second-month festival.
claims.statement_id: Menurut abstrak artikel itu, makna perayaan loy khamot adalah menghanyutkan nasib buruk dan dosa, yakni mengurangi malapetaka dalam diri agar mengalir bersama air pada perayaan bulan kedua.
claims.quote: ความสำคั ญของประเพณี ลอยโขมด เป็นการลอยเคราะห์ลอยบาป ต้องการลดเคราะห์เสนียด จัญไรในตัวให้ไหลไปตามน้ำในเทศกาลเดือนยี่

claims.statement: The mandurugo is a mythical being of Philippine folklore similar to a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Mandurugo adalah makhluk mitos dari cerita rakyat Filipina yang mirip vampir.
claims.quote: The Mandurugo is a mythical being from Philippine folklore, similar to a vampire.

claims.statement: The mandurugo, a variety of aswang, is usually a young beautiful woman by day but at night grows wings and a long sharp tongue to cut a man's neck or prick his mouth while kissing to get blood.
claims.statement_id: Mandurugo, sejenis aswang, pada siang hari biasanya perempuan muda cantik, tetapi pada malam hari menumbuhkan sayap dan lidah panjang tajam untuk melukai leher laki-laki atau menusuk mulutnya saat berciuman demi darah.
claims.quote: A variety of Aswang (Filipino shapeshifter), the Mandurugo resembles a vampire. They are usually young and beautiful women by day, but develop wings and long, sharp tongues by night, which they use to either make cuts in a man's neck, or prick the inside of his mouth while kissing him to obtain blood.

claims.statement: Its stories, popular among Tagalog and Bicol speakers, vary; sometimes it marries men to prey on them, or keeps one husband as cover and flies to other villages to feed.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya populer di kalangan penutur Tagalog dan Bicol dan bervariasi; kadang mandurugo menikahi laki-laki untuk dimangsa, atau memilih satu suami sebagai kedok lalu terbang ke desa lain untuk makan.
claims.quote: The stories, popular to Tagalog and Bicol speakers, have many variations. Sometimes the Mandurugo marries unsuspecting men to prey upon them, or may just select one husband, using him as a cover for her blood drinking activities, flying to other villages to feed.

claims.statement: In The Girl With Many Loves, the fourth husband keeps a knife, feels a prick on his neck, stabs the creature above him, and next day his wife is found dead with a knife wound in her chest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Gadis dengan Banyak Cinta, suami keempat berjaga dengan pisau, merasakan tusukan di leher, menikam makhluk di atasnya, dan esoknya istrinya ditemukan tewas dengan luka tusuk di dada.
claims.quote: The fourth husband, fearing the same fate as his predecessors, is afraid to sleep at night and holds a knife in his hand. A little after midnight, the man senses something over him before feeling a prick on his neck. He stabs at the creature on top of him and hears a loud screech and the flapping of wings. The next day, his wife is found dead

claims.statement: Films such as The Vampire People (1966) were products of vampire folklore and mainstream culture.
claims.statement_id: Film seperti The Vampire People (1966) lahir dari cerita rakyat vampir dan budaya arus utama.
claims.quote: Films such as The Vampire People (1966) were the product of vampire folklore and mainstream culture.

claims.statement: In the tale, her husband, described as an over-weight youth, withers away to bones in less than a year.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah "Gadis dengan Banyak Cinta", suaminya, seorang pemuda yang digambarkan gemuk, menyusut sampai tinggal tulang dalam waktu kurang dari setahun.
claims.quote: Her husband, described as an over-weight youth, withers away to bones in less than a year.

claims.statement: After he dies, the woman marries again and again with the same result, until she reaches her fourth husband.
claims.statement_id: Setelah suaminya meninggal, perempuan itu menikah lagi berulang kali dengan hasil yang sama sampai tiba pada suami keempat.
claims.quote: After he dies, the woman marries again and again with the same result, until she reaches her fourth husband.

claims.statement: According to the Aswang Project compendium, a precise term designating the vampire is the Tagalog word mandurugo, blood (sucker); a pretty girl in the tale "The Girl of Many Loves" proved to be a mandurugo, "blood sucker".
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompendium Aswang Project, istilah tepat untuk vampir adalah kata Tagalog mandurugo, "(penghisap) darah"; seorang gadis cantik dalam kisah "The Girl of Many Loves" ternyata mandurugo, "penghisap darah".
claims.quote: A precise term designating the vampire is the Tagalog word mandurugo, blood (sucker). A pretty girl in the tale “The Girl of Many Loves” proved to be a mandurugo, ‘blood sucker’.

claims.statement: The mandurugo is said to fly from Capiz between midnight and the first cockrow.
claims.statement_id: Konon mandurugo terbang dari Capiz antara tengah malam dan kokok ayam pertama.
claims.quote: Is said to fly from Capiz between midnight and the first cockrow.

claims.statement: The mandurugo becomes powerless at dawn and can be killed with a knife.
claims.statement_id: Mandurugo menjadi tak berdaya saat fajar dan dapat dibunuh dengan pisau.
claims.quote: Becomes powerless at dawn and can be killed with a knife.

claims.statement: According to the Wikipedia article on aswang, the vampire aswang takes on the appearance of a beautiful woman and shares a diet of blood with Western vampires, but sucks blood with a proboscis-like tongue rather than sharpened teeth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia tentang aswang, aswang vampir menyerupai perempuan cantik, memakan darah seperti vampir Barat, tetapi mengisap darah dengan lidah mirip belalai, bukan taring tajam.
claims.quote: The vampire aswang assumes on the appearance of a beautiful woman. It shares a diet of blood with vampires from Western cultures; however, it differs in that it sucks blood using a proboscis-like tongue rather than sharpened teeth.

claims.statement: The Wikipedia article on aswang gives the Tagalog mandurugo as an example of a vampire aswang, said to live in the region of Capiz.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia tentang aswang menyebut mandurugo Tagalog sebagai contoh aswang vampir, yang konon tinggal di wilayah Capiz.
claims.quote: One example of a vampire aswang is the Tagalog mandurugo, said to live in the region of Capiz.

claims.statement: According to the Wikipedia article on aswang, the vampire aswang does not reside in tombs.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia tentang aswang, aswang vampir tidak tinggal di makam.
claims.quote: Furthermore, aswang does not reside in tombs.

claims.statement: According to Maximo Ramos, "aswang" is an aggregate term for many Filipino supernatural creatures that can be organized into five categories, one of them the vampire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Maximo Ramos, istilah "aswang" adalah istilah gabungan bagi banyak makhluk gaib Filipina, yang dapat digolongkan ke dalam lima kategori, salah satunya vampir.
claims.quote: According to Maximo Ramos, the term "aswang" can be thought of as an aggregate term for a multitude of Filipino supernatural creatures. These creatures can be organized into five categories that parallel creatures from Western traditions. These categories are the vampire, the self-segmenting viscera sucker, the weredog, the witch, and the ghoul.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the anime Blade features the manananggal and the mandurugo (harpy-like), two flying variants of aswang.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, anime Blade menampilkan manananggal dan mandurugo (mirip harpi), dua varian aswang yang terbang.
claims.quote: The anime Blade features the manananggal (self-segmenting) and mandurugo (harpy-like, two flying variants of aswangs.
